2027-06-15.title: Tuesday of the Eleventh Week in Ordinary Time
readings: Though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor
Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you
2027-06-15.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 11 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green.
2027-06-15.verse: But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father in heaven; for he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the righteous and on the unrighteous.
theo: For several years St Paul organised a collection among his Gentile churches for the poor Christians of Jerusalem (Romans 15:26; 1 Corinthians 16:1–4). It mattered to him greatly: it was a sign that Jews and Gentiles in Christ were one family. In today's reading he tells the Corinthians, who were fairly prosperous, about the churches of Macedonia, Philippi and Thessalonica, who were not: “during a severe ordeal of affliction, their abundant joy and their extreme poverty have overflowed in a wealth of generosity on their part.” Poverty and joy together produced generosity. “They voluntarily gave according to their means, and even beyond their means, begging us earnestly for the privilege of sharing in this ministry to the saints.” The poor begged for the privilege of giving! And Paul gives the secret: “they gave themselves first to the Lord.” When the heart is given, the purse follows. Paul does not command the Corinthians; he invites them to “excel also in this generous undertaking,” and then he points to the source of all giving: “For you know the generous act of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, so that by his poverty you might become rich.” The word Paul uses for this “generous act” is charis, grace. The Son of God emptied himself, was born in a manger and died on a cross, and by his poverty we receive the riches of God. The Psalm sings of the same God, “who executes justice for the oppressed; who gives food to the hungry.”

In the Gospel Jesus reaches the summit of the Sermon on the Mount. “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’” The Law of Moses commanded love of neighbour (Leviticus 19:18); nowhere did it command hatred of enemies, but many concluded that a neighbour meant only one's own people, and that enemies could be hated. Jesus breaks that boundary: “But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father in heaven.” And he gives the reason from the sky itself: the Father “makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the righteous and on the unrighteous.” In these monsoon weeks we see it with our own eyes: the rain does not ask whose field it is falling on. To love only those who love us is no more than “the tax collectors” do; to greet only our own is what everyone does. Then comes the great command: “Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.” The Greek word, teleios, means complete, mature, whole. St Luke gives the same saying as “Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful” (Luke 6:36). The perfection of the Father is not a cold flawlessness; it is mercy without limits. Every Christian, and not only priests and religious, is called to this holiness (Lumen Gentium 40).
outline: Ask: who is the hardest person for me to pray for? Have I ever prayed for them by name?
The poor Macedonians give beyond their means because they gave themselves first to the Lord.
Point 2 · Sun and rain for all
The Father's love does not choose; ours must not either.
Point 3 · Be perfect as your Father
The perfection of the Father is mercy; all are called to holiness.
“Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.”
live: Before you give money or time today, give yourself to the Lord in a short prayer, and then give gladly.
Pray today by name for one person who has hurt you, asking God to bless them.
2027-06-15.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, though you were rich, yet for our sakes you became poor, so that by your poverty we might become rich. Give us the joy of the churches of Macedonia, who gave beyond their means because they gave themselves first to you. Father in heaven, you make your sun rise on the evil and on the good and send your rain on all; teach us to love our enemies and to pray for those who persecute us, so that we may truly be your children, merciful as you are merciful. Amen.
altar: In the Eucharist the generous act of our Lord Jesus Christ is made present: he who was rich became poor, and now he gives himself under the poor signs of bread and wine. At the altar he prays for those who persecuted him, “Father, forgive them,” and the sacrifice of the cross is offered for friend and enemy alike. Whoever receives him receives a heart that can love enemies.

quick: Paul tells the Corinthians how the poor churches of Macedonia gave with joy, beyond their means, because they first gave themselves to the Lord.
The model of all giving is Christ, who though he was rich became poor for our sakes, so that by his poverty we might become rich.
Jesus commands: love your enemies, pray for your persecutors, and be perfect as your heavenly Father is perfect.
2027-06-15.action: Pray by name today for someone who has hurt you, and ask God to bless them.
2027-06-15.question: Does my love stop at the edge of my own family and friends, or does it reach, like the rain, to those who do not love me?

family.explain: Look out of the window when it rains. The rain falls on every house, every field, every tree. It does not ask: is this a good person or a bad person? Jesus says God loves like that. He sends the sun and the rain on everyone. And he asks us to love like that too, even people who are not kind to us, and to pray for them.
family.intention: We pray for people who have hurt our family, and for families that are not speaking to each other.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we find hard to love? Can we say a prayer for them together tonight?”

illus: Sister Rani Maria Vattalil, a Franciscan Clarist sister from Kerala, worked among the poor in Madhya Pradesh. In 1995 she was stabbed to death on a bus by a man hired by those who resented her work. Years later her own sister, Sister Selmy Paul, visited the murderer, Samundar Singh, in prison and tied a rakhi on his wrist, the thread that makes him a brother. Her family forgave him, and he came to repent and was present at Sister Rani Maria's beatification in Indore in 2017. Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you. (A true story.)

pm.open: Praise the Lord, O my soul! You make your sun rise on the evil and on the good. Make our hearts as wide as yours. Amen.
share: They gave themselves first to the Lord (2 Corinthians 8:5). Have I given myself to the Lord, or only some of my things?
Though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor (2 Corinthians 8:9). How has Christ made me rich?
Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you (Matthew 5:44). Whom do I need to pray for today?
interc: For the poor, and for all who share generously with them out of their own little.
For those who persecute Christians in India and in the world, that their hearts may be changed.
For families and neighbours divided by old enmities.
For farmers waiting for the rain, and for those who suffer from floods.
For our group, that we may love as the Father loves.
pm.close: Father, your Son became poor to make us rich and taught us to love our enemies. Make us your children in deed and in truth. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul tells a beautiful story about the churches of Macedonia. They were poor and suffering, yet their abundant joy and their extreme poverty have overflowed in a wealth of generosity (2 Corinthians 8:2). They even begged Paul for the privilege of giving! How is that possible? Paul says: they gave themselves first to the Lord (2 Corinthians 8:5). When we belong to God, giving becomes a joy.

And Paul shows us where this generosity comes from: you know the generous act of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, so that by his poverty you might become rich (2 Corinthians 8:9). Jesus left the glory of heaven, was born in a stable, and died with nothing. Everything we have of God, we have because he became poor for us.

In the Gospel Jesus asks the hardest thing of all: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you (Matthew 5:44). Look at the monsoon rain. It falls on the field of the good farmer and of the lazy one, on the church and on the toddy shop. Jesus says: that is how your Father loves. He makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good. If we love only those who love us, what is special about that?

Our Church in India knows such love. Blessed Rani Maria was killed in 1995, and her family forgave her murderer and welcomed him as a brother. That is what Jesus means by: be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect (Matthew 5:48). Not a perfection of never making mistakes, but a perfection of mercy. Let us ask today for this grace: to pray, by name, for one person who has hurt us. Amen.
kids: Children, when it rains, does the rain fall only on good children's houses? No! It falls on everyone. Jesus says God loves everyone like that. And he asks us to love even people who are not nice to us. Is there someone at school who teases you? Tonight, say a little prayer for them: Jesus, bless my friend. That is a very brave and beautiful thing to do.

intro: Theme: “Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.”
The generosity of the poor, the poverty of Christ that makes us rich, and the Father's love that falls like rain on all.

sub: Joy and poverty overflowing in generosity.
The generous act of our Lord.
q: who executes justice for the oppressed; who gives food to the hungry.
For you know the generous act of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, so that by his poverty you might become rich.
points.apply: Give something this week from your own need, not only from what you have left over, and give it with joy.

sub: The Father's love does not choose.
q: When you come upon your enemy's ox or donkey going astray, you shall bring it back.
But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father in heaven;
points.apply: Do one practical kindness this week for someone who does not like you.

sub: Merciful as the Father is merciful.
Every Christian is called to holiness.
q: You shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy.
Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
points.apply: Each evening this week ask: where was I merciful today, and where did I fail to be?

concl: The poor of Macedonia gave beyond their means because they had first given themselves; Christ became poor to make us rich.
The Father's love falls like rain on all; we become his children when we love our enemies and pray for those who hurt us.
2027-06-15.resolve: Pray every day this week, by name, for one person who has hurt you.
